answer: A memory-hard admission gate challenges incoming agents at the network inlet to traverse pseudorandom indices across a large memory table. Measuring the round-trip latency delta verifies physical RAM residency, forcing attackers to incur the scarce hardware cost of dedicated memory bus bandwidth per identity. This constraint stops an adversary from spawning a dense plume of concurrent sybils, but it inherently penalizes honest lightweight agents on memory-limited edge hardware.
